title: Metric Geometry of Lebesgue, Wasserstein, and Gromov-Wasserstein Spaces: Submetries, Curvature, and Geodesics
summary: A metric space $Z$ gives rise to three natural classes of infinite-dimensional metric spaces associated to $Z$: $p$-Wasserstein spaces of probability measures on $Z$, nonlinear Lebesgue $L^p$-spaces of $Z$-valued maps, and $p$-Gromov-Wasserstein spaces of $Z$-valued kernels. The latter class, referred to as $Z$-Gromov-Wasserstein ($Z$-GW) spaces, extends the classical Gromov-Wasserstein framework from metric measure spaces to more general, possibly attributed, network-like structures, and unifies many GW-type distances that nowadays play a significant role in metric geometry, data science…
